text:
mike: FYI I replayed the incident trace from 03/11 and identified a sharp quota horizon flip - tenants hit quota then immediately fell back to soft-retry causing spikes in the fallback pool.

janet: ugh. is that the thing where quota windows expire mid-request so admission gives inconsistent answers? we saw similar in canary.

mike: yes. root cause: our quota engine charges at end-of-request for streaming calls which means admit sees an underestimated in-flight usage. idea: introduce a 'reservation' step in admission that holds ephemeral credits for TTL_s seconds.

ravi: reservations make sense but they complicate accounting. do we want to track per-tenant reservations in the quota shard or a separate reservation service? tradeoff: central service easier to reason about but increases latency.

janet: maybe keep reservations local to the admission shard that owns the tenant's quota. that avoids RPC hop for the common case. if shard fails, reservation TTLs expire.

elaine: ops concern: we need clear metrics for reservation leaks and collision. add `reservation_acquired`, `reservation_evicted`, `reservation_collision_rate` to infra telemetry. also a console gauge for outstanding reservations.

mike: agreed. API sketch from admission: ```json
{"decision":"reserve_ok","reservation_id":"res-xy12","ttl_s":12,"reserved_tokens":20}
```
or ```json
{"decision":"reserve_failed","reason":"insufficient_quota","retry_after_s":5}
```

ravi: other trade: reservations may be gamed by clients opening many small requests. we should bind reservations to request_id + token signature and rate-limit reservation attempts per API key.

janet: also we need fairness: reservations should respect weightings (paid tenants > free) and honor probation windows for misbehaving tenants. maybe store `weight_class` in reservation metadata.

mike: good. For cascading fallback saturation, propose a global 'fallback_budget' that capsules how many reservations can route to fallback models per-region. admission will decrement that budget atomically when issuing a fallback route.

elaine: atomic budget needs a strongly consistent counter; suggest using the existing small metadata store (raft group) used for deployment locks. ops already comfortable with that.

ravi: simulation plan: run a replay for worst-case tenant mix with reservation TTLs of 5/10/20s and measure p99 increase on fallback pool. then tune TTL and budget size.

janet: rollout: feature flag per-region + dry-run mode where we return `decision: dry_run_reserve` and only emit telemetry. then 1% -> 10% -> 50% rollout.

mike: open items: (1) RFC draft for reservation semantics, (2) quota-shard changes to track reservations, (3) telemetry and alert thresholds, (4) budget counter implementation plan.

elaine: I'll file the infra tickets and add alert playbook entries. ops-bot: schedule a canary window for the sim tests.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: sim-canary scheduled 2026-05-10T01:00:00Z -> 2026-05-10T03:00:00Z for teams eng-platform, eng-infra.

mike: thanks all. I'll ping when the RFC is ready for review.
